title: Bug: Fizz image preload headers drop referrerPolicy for rendered
body: React version: current `main` (`c014813413`) ## Steps To Reproduce 1. Render with `renderToPipeableStream` and provide an `onHeaders` callback. 2. Render an image like ``. 3. Inspect the `Link` header captured by `onHeaders`. Link to code example: Minimal repro inline: ```js let headers = null; function onHeaders(x) { headers = x; } renderToPipeableStream( , {onHeaders}, ); console.log(headers.Link); ``` ## The current behavior When the preload is emitted as an HTTP `Link` header, `referrerpolicy` is missing. The fallback `` path does preserve `referrerPolicy`, so the behavior changes depending on whether the preload is emitted as a header or as a DOM node. ## The expected behavior If the rendered image preload includes `referrerPolicy`, the same value should be preserved in the emitted `Link` header. I opened a small fix here as well: #36561.

title: Add block-no-verify PreToolUse hook to .claude/settings.json
body:
## Feature: Add block-no-verify PreToolUse hook to .claude/settings.json

React's `.claude/settings.json` already has a `SessionStart` hook for instructions and a well-configured permissions list. There's one enforcement gap worth closing: the git hook-bypass flag.

When Claude Code runs `git commit` or `git push` with the hook-bypass flag, it silently skips pre-commit hooks, commit-msg validation, and pre-push test suites — regardless of any permissions or quality gates configured elsewhere.

### Proposed fix

Add `block-no-verify@1.1.2` ([github.com/tupe12334/block-no-verify](https://github.com/tupe12334/block-no-verify)) as a `PreToolUse` Bash hook alongside the existing `SessionStart` hook:

```json
"PreToolUse": [
  {
    "matcher": "Bash",
    "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "npx block-no-verify@1.1.2" }]
  }
]
```

**Note:** The existing config denies `Bash(npx:*)` — this applies to what Claude Code can run through its Bash tool, but hooks run as system-level shell commands outside that permission scope. So the hook will run correctly.

The package reads `tool_input.command` from the Claude Code hook stdin, detects the hook-bypass flag across all git subcommands, and exits 2 to block. All existing hooks and permissions are preserved unchanged.

---

_Disclosure: I am the author and maintainer of `block-no-verify`._

title: react-reconciler: flushSync was renamed to flushSyncFromReconciler without deprecation notice
body:
In react-reconciler, the `flushSync` export was renamed to `flushSyncFromReconciler` in PR #28500 (merged April 8, 2024). This is an undocumented breaking change for custom renderers.

**Commit:** https://github.com/facebook/react/pull/28500

According to that PR, custom renderers should now use:
- `reconciler.updateContainerSync()` - to update synchronously
- `reconciler.flushSyncWork()` - to flush pending sync work

However, this migration path is not documented anywhere for custom renderer authors. The change silently causes `flushSync` to be `undefined` with no warning.

**0.29.x API:**
```js
const reconciler = ReactReconciler(hostConfig)
const { flushSync } = reconciler  // works

// Usage
flushSync(() => {
  reconciler.updateContainer(element, container, null, callback)
})
```

**0.31.0+ API:**
```js
const reconciler = ReactReconciler(hostConfig)
const { flushSync } = reconciler  // undefined!

// New intended usage (undocumented):
reconciler.updateContainerSync(element, container, null, callback)
reconciler.flushSyncWork()
```

Could we please:
1. Document the new API for custom renderers in the react-reconciler README
2. Or add a deprecation warning when accessing the old `flushSync` property

This affects custom renderers like @opentui/react that were following the previous patterns.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. clone https://github.com/Yovach/deno-tanstack-start-bug-reproduction
2. deno install
3. deno task build


## The current behavior

It's hanging forever.

## The expected behavior

Not hanging on `deno task build`


## Context

I've been investigating the vite build hanging issue in Deno and found the root cause. https://github.com/denoland/deno/issues/31248

Seems that `react-dom` package.json maps Deno to use the browser bundle (`server.browser.js`) instead of the node bundle. The browser bundle creates a MessageChannel for task scheduling, and this MessageChannel keeps Deno's process alive forever, causing the hang.
Runtime mappings:
  • Node.js → uses `setImmediate` from server.node.js (doesn't block exit) :white_check_mark:
  • Bun → uses `queueMicrotask` from server.bun.js (doesn't block exit) :white_check_mark:
  • Deno → uses `MessageChannel` from server.browser.js (blocks exit forever) :x:

## Solutions

Changing the "deno" mapping from `"./server.browser.js"` to `"./server.node.js"` at `node_modules/.deno/react-dom@19.2.0/node_modules/react-dom/package.json` fixed the hang.

title: [Compiler: suggestion] Performance improvement: Replace template literals with single quotes for static strings
body:
Dear React Compiler team,

I would like to bring to your attention a potential performance consideration regarding the current code generation strategy.

The React Compiler consistently uses template literals (backticks) for all string literals in the generated code, even when no variable interpolation is needed. For example:

```javascript
// Current output
(0, Z.jsxs)(`p`, {
    children: [
        `Edit `,
        (0, Z.jsx)(`code`, { children: `src/App.tsx` }),
        ` and save to test HMR`,
    ],
})

// Could be optimized to
(0, Z.jsxs)('p', {
    children: [
        'Edit ',
        (0, Z.jsx)('code', { children: 'src/App.tsx' }),
        ' and save to test HMR',
    ],
})
```

While the performance difference is minimal for individual string operations, template literals have a slight overhead compared to regular string literals due to:
- Additional parsing for potential interpolation syntax
- Slightly larger memory footprint
- More complex string creation process

Proposal:
- Uses single quotes for static strings without interpolation
- Only uses template literals when actual variable interpolation is needed

Tools:
- "vite": "npm:rolldown-vite@latest"
- "babel-plugin-react-compiler": "^1.0.0"

title: Bug: Massive memory allocations using React dev build under frequent updates (prod build unaffected)

title: Bug: Using the new <Activity> component inside AnimatePresence (Framer Motion)
body:
React version: 19.2.0

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Wrap a component in the new React <Activity> component for conditional visibility:

`<Activity mode="visible">
  <Component />
</Activity>
`

2. Try to animate this visibility change using Framer Motion’s <AnimatePresence>:

`<AnimatePresence>
  <Activity mode={open ? "visible" : "hidden"}>
    <motion.div exit={{ opacity: 0 }}>
      <Component />
    </motion.div>
  </Activity>
</AnimatePresence>
`

Observe that AnimatePresence expects children to be conditionally rendered (e.g., {open && <Component />}) for enter/exit animations to trigger.

## The current behavior

When wrapping motion elements with <Activity>, Framer Motion’s AnimatePresence does not detect mounting/unmounting changes — because <Activity> toggles visibility internally (using display: none and subscription unmounting) instead of actually adding/removing children from the React tree.
As a result, exit animations do not trigger.

## The expected behavior

Ideally, <Activity> would expose some API or compatibility layer to integrate with animation libraries like Framer Motion that depend on conditional rendering for entry/exit transitions — or React could provide guidance on how to handle this scenario correctly.

title: eslint-plugin-react-hooks needs dependency on zod ^3.25.0 or later
body:
https://github.com/facebook/react/blob/ac3e705a18696168acfcaed39dce0cfaa6be8836/packages/eslint-plugin-react-hooks/package.json#L46

eslint-plugin-react-hooks currently has these dependencies:

```json
  "dependencies": {
    ...
    "zod": "^3.22.4",
    "zod-validation-error": "^3.0.3"
  },
```

More recent versions of zod-validation-plugin since 3.5.3 (matched by "^3.0.3" above) have a peer-dependency requirement for `"zod": "^3.25.0 || ^4.0.0"`, and they are internally using the zod/v3 import introduced by zod 3.25.0.

eslint-plugin-react-hooks should change its dependencies to:

```json
    "zod": "^3.25.0",
    "zod-validation-error": "^3.5.3"
```

Or maybe go all the way to the latest versions of both packages.

Currently, when using `use()` in React server components, if a server-side action fails or is unavailable, it may fall back to executing on the client side. I propose adding a parameter or option that allows developers to **disallow this fallback**, ensuring that certain actions always remain server-only.

This would be useful in scenarios where:

* Sensitive operations must never execute on the client.
* Server-specific resources or data are required.
* Consistency and security need to be enforced.

* Add a boolean parameter (e.g., `allowClientFallback = true`) to `use()`.
* When set to `false`, `use()` should throw an error if the server action is unavailable, instead of falling back to client-side execution.

**Example:**

```js
const data = use(fetchServerData, { allowClientFallback: false });
```

**Benefits:**

* Prevent accidental execution of server-only logic on the client.
* Improve security and predictability of server components.
* Give developers explicit control over fallback behavior.

## Summary

I propose that every `react` root be automatically wrapped in a `Suspense` boundary with no fallback
UI.

```diff
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { App } from './app';

const element = document.getElementById('root');
const root = createRoot(element);

root.render(
+ // Suspense boundary with no fallback UI added by react internally

+  </Suspense>
);

title: [Compiler]: Memoization not applying
body:
### What kind of issue is this?

- [x] React Compiler core (the JS output is incorrect, or your app works incorrectly after optimization)
- [ ] babel-plugin-react-compiler (build issue installing or using the Babel plugin)
- [ ] eslint-plugin-react-compiler (build issue installing or using the eslint plugin)
- [ ] react-compiler-healthcheck (build issue installing or using the healthcheck script)

### Link to repro

https://github.com/OliverJAsh/react-compiler-flow-bug

### Repro steps

The reduced test case contains two components, `WithFlow` and `WithoutFlow`. They are identical except for this line:

`WithFlow`:
```js
const myRef = flow((x) => [x], setState);
```
`WithoutFlow`:
```js
const myRef = (x) => {
  setState([x]);
};
```

For reference, `flow` is a helper function for composing functions together:

```js
const flow = (a, b) => (x) => b(a(x));
```

When using `WithFlow` we get `Maximum update depth exceeded.`.

When using `WithoutFlow` it works (no error).

---

### Vue version

3.5.29

### Link to minimal reproduction

N/A (Nuxt project, see steps below)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a Nuxt 4 project using `vue@3.5.28` — `nuxi typecheck` passes

```
Property '$route' does not exist on type '{ ... $nuxt: NuxtApp; }'
Property 'navigateTo' does not exist on type '{ ... $nuxt: NuxtApp; }'
```

3. Pin back to `vue@3.5.28` — passes again

Reproduced with:
- vue-tsc 3.2.5
- nuxt 4.3.1
- typescript 5.9.3

The issue affects any property added to templates via `ComponentCustomProperties` augmentation (e.g. `$route` from vue-router, `navigateTo` from Nuxt).

### What is expected?

`ComponentCustomProperties` augmentations (like `$route` from vue-router) should be recognized in templates during type checking, as they are in 3.5.28.

### What is actually happening?

Template type checking no longer sees properties added via `ComponentCustomProperties` module augmentation. All uses of `$route`, `navigateTo`, etc. in `<template>` produce TS2339 errors.

### System Info

```
macOS Darwin 25.3.0 (ARM64)
Ubuntu 24.04 ARM (GitHub Actions)
bun 1.3.10
```

### Any additional comments?

Pinning `vue` to `3.5.28` is a workaround. The regression was bisected by swapping only the vue version in a Nuxt 4 project — all other dependencies held constant.

- use the compiled component within a recent version of vue eg. 3.5.27

### What is expected?

This shouldn't break the behaviour of the "old" vue customElement.

### What is actually happening?

The recent renderer of vue think that the customElement is based on the same version of vue and try to call some optimized inexsitant methods on it.

### Any additional comments?

I believe that adding a safe fallback (optional chaining or check if methods exists), should be simple enough to fix the bug.

```js
if (customElement._beginPatch) {
    customElement._beginPatch()
}

// or

if (customElement) {
    customElement?._beginPatch()
}
```

body:
### Version
3.5.22

### Reproduction link
[play.vuejs.org/](https://play.vuejs.org/#__SSR__)


### Steps to reproduce
Load the page so that Vue hydrates the SSR HTML.

### What is expected?
Similar to [HTML parsing](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#preprocessing-the-input-stream), I expect Vue to [normalize newlines](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#normalize-newlines) by replacing every CRLF with a LF and then replace every remaining CR with a LF.

Vue renders the CRLF on the server as is. During hydration, Vue expects CRLF on the client. But the browser has replaced the CRLF with LF during parsing, causing a hydration mismatch.

title: Replace lodash with es-toolkit/compat for smaller bundle size and better tree-shaking
body:
### What problem does this feature solve?
Currently, Vue core uses lodash in some internal utilities. While lodash is a powerful and widely used library, it has a relatively large footprint and does not tree-shake well, especially when full imports or deep utilities are used.

In modern JavaScript projects, bundle size is a major performance concern, particularly for frontend libraries. In one of my recent projects, lodash was contributing around 145kb to the final bundle after minification.

es-toolkit is a lightweight, modular alternative that offers tree-shakable utility functions with a similar API to lodash. Migrating to es-toolkit/compat can reduce bundle size and modernize the dependency stack with no changes to developer-facing APIs.

This change could help Vue align better with modern ecosystem practices and further optimize its performance for end users.

### What does the proposed API look like?
The migration would be internal only — swapping out lodash utilities with es-toolkit/compat equivalents. No public API changes are involved.

Here is a simple example:

```ts
// Current
const uniq = require('lodash.uniq')

// Proposed
const { uniq } = require('es-toolkit/compat/uniq')
```
This keeps the usage pattern the same while replacing the underlying dependency.
Tests will be run to ensure behavior consistency. I'd be happy to raise a PR and evaluate the size and performance impact of this migration.

This is a critical issue for any type of web component that provides users with interactions. It blocks proper keyboard navigation and programmatic focusing of elements.

When creating custom web components that have focus-able parts (like inputs or buttons) the focus is first set to the custom element itself. That is why, in the example provided, the outline is showing for the entire element instead of the input.

title: Allow <keep-alive> to act like v-show
body:
### What problem does this feature solve?
In a single page app.
Trying to use <keep-alive> to keep a <router-view> alive that displays long lists of items has a lower performance than manually handling the component visibility with `v-show`.

Currently, using <keep-alive> in combination with <router-view> causes the UI to freeze as it still re-renders the list items when switching between routes. (Yes, it was implemented correctly as shown [here](https://router.vuejs.org/guide/advanced/router-view-slot))

Having a way for the <keep-alive> component to simply hide the kept alive components the same way that `v-show` does would allow me to use the it in combination with <router-view> and keep the same performance improvements I currently have with v-show.

### What does the proposed API look like?
A component prop like `<keep-alive strategy="[some strategy option]">` would be perfect.

Not sure of the option names, but something that would allow us to decide between the "classic" keep alive strategy and the `v-show` strategy.

title: Generic Type Constraints with null | undefined Are Stripped During Build
body:
### Vue version

3.4.21

### Link to minimal reproduction

https://play.vuejs.org/#

### Steps to reproduce

```
<script setup lang="ts" generic="V extends string | number | null | undefined">
import {ref} from "vue";

const value = ref<V>(null)
</script>

<template>
  <input v-model="value" />
</template>
```
Then run `npm run build`.

The built output only includes `<V extends string | number>`, dropping the `null | undefined` constraints.

### What is expected?

The generic type constraint should preserve `null | undefined` types
Component should accept `null/undefined` values when used with appropriate type parameters

### What is actually happening?

Built output strips `null | undefined` from generic constraints
TypeScript errors occur when trying to pass null values to components, even though they're explicitly included in the constraints

title: animate.leave skipped for the closing panel when switching panels in an exclusive accordion (sibling instances share a TNode)
body:
> **TL;DR — it breaks an exclusive accordion.** In an accordion (or tab group / expandable nav menu) where opening one panel closes the currently-open one, clicking a different panel makes the open panel **disappear instantly instead of animating its `animate.leave` collapse**. The opening panel's `animate.enter` plays fine; only the *closing* panel is broken, and only when another opens in the same change-detection tick.
>
> It's **order-dependent**: it only breaks when the closing section comes *before* the opening one in DOM order. (Both sections update in one tick, in order — so the closing element is detached and tracked *first*, then the entering sibling cancels it.) Closing a *later* section while opening an *earlier* one animates fine, as does toggling a single section with nothing else opening. So in the repro, **clicking Section B while A is open is broken; clicking Section A while B is open animates correctly** — don't be fooled by trying the working direction.
>
> Why: the panels are separate instances of the **same** item component, so their animated elements share one `TNode`. `cancelLeavingNodes` (added in 21.2.0) sees the still-animating closing panel under that shared `TNode` in a different DOM parent, assumes it's a stale duplicate, and force-removes it.
>
> ▶️ **Repro — same code, side by side** (a two-section exclusive accordion; click **Section B** while **Section A** is open):

title: Security regression: SVG <a [attr.href]> skips URL sanitizer in 22.0.0-rc.1 (@next) and main HEAD
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

compiler, core

### Is this a regression?

Yes

### Description

## TLDR

After the namespace-aware schema lookup refactor on `main` (commits `cef4a095`, `61a97f22`, `933608c0`), the security schema lookup for `<svg><a [attr.href]>` returns `SecurityContext.NONE` instead of `SecurityContext.URL`. The compiler emits `ɵɵattribute("href", value)` **without** the `ɵɵsanitizeUrl` wrap. Same template on `22.0.0-rc.0` emitted the sanitizer correctly.

**As of 2026-05-25 the bug is present in `@angular/compiler@22.0.0-rc.1` published on npm with the `@next` dist-tag** — confirmed by fresh empirical compile (witness below). Anyone running `npm install @angular/compiler@next` is exposed.

End result on a built app : a `<svg><a [attr.href]="userHref">` binding accepts a `javascript:` URL verbatim and writes it to the DOM `href` attribute. A user click navigates to the `javascript:` URL → script execution in the app's origin → XSS in modern Chrome.

This is the same class of bug that CVE-2025-66412 closed for MathML `<mi href>`, re-introduced for SVG anchors by the schema rework.

title: `<noscript>` text serialization in Angular SSR
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

platform-server/domino

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

When Angular SSR (`@angular/platform-server`, which uses `@angular/domino`) renders text inside a `<noscript>` element via `{{ value }}` or `[textContent]`, the value is written to the SSR response **without escaping**.

If the value contains `</noscript>`, the noscript element closes early in the HTML sent to the browser, and any markup after it  including `<script>` is parsed and executed normally, same-origin.

Text bindings (`{{ }}`, `[textContent]`) are assumed safe by developers. They are not safe inside `<noscript>` under SSR.

title: Unvalidated JSONP Resource URL in Angular `HttpClient`
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

common/http

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description


`HttpClient.jsonp()` accepts a caller-provided URL and loads it as a JSONP script resource.

If an application enables JSONP support and passes attacker-controlled input directly into `http.jsonp()`, for example from the current page URL:

```ts
const jsonpUrl = new URL(location.href).searchParams.get('jsonpUrl');
this.http.jsonp(jsonpUrl!, 'callback').subscribe();
```

then a crafted link can cause the browser to execute an attacker-controlled JSONP resource in the Angular application context.

For example, if `jsonpUrl` is a `data:text/javascript,...` resource, the loaded script executes before invoking Angular’s generated JSONP callback.

Angular should reject or restrict unsafe JSONP resource URLs before creating the script element. At minimum, non-HTTP(S) protocols such as `data:`, `blob:`, `javascript:`, `file:`, and `filesystem:` should not be accepted as JSONP script resources.


### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug
 
This issue was previously reported to the Google VRP. The original PoV and discussion can be seen here, if accessible: https://issuetracker.google.com/u/1/issues/510947871

### Anything else?

If we consider Angular's model, which is secure by default, I believe it shouldn't allow it unless we explicitly want to perform a bypass.

title: Angular service worker bypasses explicit `redirect: 'error'`, leaks authenticated content into JavaScript, and replays it after logout.
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

service-worker

### Description

Details
Angular service worker asset handling reconstructs outgoing requests through AssetGroup.newRequestWithMetadata() while preserving headers only. In the redirected asset path, this drops explicit redirect policy from the original request. As a result, a caller-supplied fetch(..., {redirect: 'error'}) is turned into a redirect-following request inside the framework service worker.

The root cause is in Angular-owned code:

packages/service-worker/worker/src/assets.ts
AssetGroup.fetchFromNetwork() manually follows redirected responses
AssetGroup.newRequestWithMetadata() rebuilds requests without preserving explicit redirect
This is a framework-owned request-policy bypass, not generic stale-cache behavior, because the browser's original decision is to reject the request and Angular service worker changes that outcome.

Attack scenario
Any actor who can get a victim to open a normal page or deep link that causes the Angular application itself to fetch the public asset URL can exploit this behavior in an Angular application that uses the Angular service worker on the affected scope and has a same-origin redirect from a public asset path to authenticated/private content. The attack does not need injected JavaScript in the victim origin if the app already performs the asset fetch on page load or route change.

title: SSRF Bypass via Absolute-Form URLs in Core Rendering APIs
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

platform-server

### Is this a regression?

Yes

### Description

The `parseUrl` function in `ServerPlatformLocation` (`packages/platform-server/src/location.ts`) was recently updated to block SSRF via protocol-relative (`//evil.com`) and backslash (`/\evil.com`) URLs by checking whether the URL string starts with `/`. If it does, the server origin is prepended before parsing.

This check does not cover HTTP/1.1 absolute-form request targets.

Per RFC 7230, a client can send a request where the full URL is the request target:

```
GET http://evil.com/ HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost
```

When Nginx, AWS ALB, or any standard reverse proxy forwards this to Node.js, Express receives `req.url = "http://evil.com/"`. That string starts with `h`, not `/`, so the guard condition `urlStr[0] === '/'` evaluates to false. The origin is not prepended. `new URL("http://evil.com/")` parses cleanly and assigns `evil.com` as `ServerPlatformLocation.hostname`.

From that point, the SSR HTTP interceptor (`relativeUrlsTransformerInterceptorFn` in `http.ts`) treats `evil.com` as the base for all relative `HttpClient` requests made during rendering. A call to `/api/config` inside the Angular component goes out as `http://evil.com/api/config` — to an external server — silently, server-side, with no error thrown and no CSR fallback triggered.

title: [Signal Forms] What should happen when submit() is called on a submitting() field?
body:
Currently, `submit()` marks the field as submitting, awaits the submit action, then finally marks the field as _not_ submitting:

https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/09b9a62a25a8f8abf9ef21dfe8a17b4135badd3f/packages/forms/signals/src/api/structure.ts#L417-L429

Consequently, if a second `submit()` call is made while one is pending, the first submission action to resolve will mark the field as _not_ submitting, despite the fact that the other action is still pending. Finally, when the last action resolves, it'll overwrite the previous submission results (errors, validity).

What _should_ be the behavior? Should we track all pending submit actions and derived the `submitting()` state from that? Should we prevent subsequent submits while pending?

title: perf(compiler): reuse temporary variable slots across non-overlapping safe navigation expressions
body:
## Problem

The Angular template compiler generates one `let` declaration per safe navigation temporary variable, even when their live ranges do not overlap. This means templates with multiple safe navigation chains produce redundant variable declarations in the compiled output.

For example, a template like:

```html
{{ a()?.b }} {{ c()?.d }}
```

currently compiles to something like:

```js
let tmp_0_0, tmp_1_0;
// ...
tmp_0_0 = ctx.a(), tmp_0_0 == null ? null : tmp_0_0.b
tmp_1_0 = ctx.c(), tmp_1_0 == null ? null : tmp_1_0.d
```

The two expressions are evaluated sequentially — `tmp_0_0` is dead by the time `tmp_1_0` is assigned — but the compiler does not detect this and allocates a separate slot for each.

This is explicitly called out in the compiler source as a known gap:

> `packages/compiler/src/template/pipeline/src/phases/temporary_variables.ts:18`
>
> ```
> // TODO: Sometimes, it will be possible to reuse names across different subexpressions. For example,
> // in the double keyed read `a?.[f()]?.[f()]`, the two function calls have non-overlapping scopes.
> // Implement an algorithm for reuse.
> ```

## Solution

{

```

title: Signal forms: Include debounce duration in pending status
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

forms

### Description

The new debounce option for `validateAsync` for signal forms is great. However, it is currently not exposed that the debounce is running as the pending state on the form field only reflects the pending nature of the validation.

Take this example, https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-qwmbwmbi?file=src%2Fmain.ts, and type in the input field. Notice that the field only switches to pending once you stop typing for a second and the debounce duration completes. 

Similarly, the error state only disappears after the debounce duration despite the error state being associated with previous value that is no longer present.

At the same time the debounced resource that is used internally and, therefore, its status is not accessible:

### Proposed solution

Consider the validation of the form field already during the debounce duration as pending. 

Additionally, this would improve the correlation between the current form value and error state as the error will immediately disappear if the user changes the form value and not keep considering the already adjusted value invalid during the debounce duration.

title: Pseudo host wrapper element
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

_No response_

### Description

Angular components don’t currently provide a way to express host-element styling and bindings *in the template* using normal element syntax. Instead, developers must use either:

- `:host` / `:host(...)` selectors in component CSS, or
- host bindings (`host: { ... }`, `@HostBinding()`, etc.).

This can be awkward in practice, especially with utility-first CSS approaches (e.g. TailwindCSS), where teams prefer to keep styling colocated with markup in the HTML template:

- `:host` pushes host styling into CSS, away from the template where most utility classes live.
- Host bindings are written differently than standard template bindings, which makes them feel inconsistent and less discoverable during refactors.
- For dynamic styling (classes/styles/attrs on the host), there’s no way to write it with the same binding syntax used for other elements in the template.

A template-level “pseudo host wrapper” would allow developers to express host attributes/classes/styles using the same syntax as any other element, while keeping the rendered DOM unchanged.


### Proposed solution

Introduce a **pseudo host element** (name bikesheddable; e.g. `<ng-host>`) that is allowed in component templates and is treated as compile-time sugar for host bindings.

Example syntax:

```html
<ng-host class="flex flex-col" [style.width.px]="calculateWidth()">
  <!-- component content -->
</ng-host... [TRUNCATED]

title: Align `ApplicationRef.bootstrap` contract with `createComponent` function
body:
Currently, the `ApplicationRef.bootstrap` function ([link](https://angular.dev/api/core/ApplicationRef#bootstrap)) has a different (more limited) set of arguments and we can extend it to support directives and bindings in a way similar to the `createComponent` function ([link](https://angular.dev/api/core/createComponent)). For symmetry, it'd be great to have the `ApplicationRef.bootstrap` function take 2 arguments:

- Component (or component factory for backwards compatibility) as the first argument
- Config object (similar to `createComponent`, but more limited) as the second argument

The tricky part would be to support the second argument in the proposed shape, since currently the second argument of the `ApplicationRef.bootstrap` function might be an object as well. This might require a breaking change and a migration.

title: NG0205 thrown on destroyed injector during SSR is unactionable in production monitoring
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

common

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

When an HTTP request is initiated after the Angular injector has been destroyed (e.g. during SSR teardown, or via a third-party SDK that captures HttpClient and fires async callbacks), Angular throws NG0205: Injector has already been destroyed.
While this error is intentional, it is unactionable in production because:

- The stack trace is fully minified — no readable symbols or context
- The request URL is never included in the error, which is the one piece of runtime information that would identify the culprit
- It is impossible to determine from the trace alone whether the call originated from your own code or a third-party dependency

This makes the error controversial in production monitoring tools (Rollbar, Sentry, Datadog) — you know something went wrong, but you cannot determine what, where, or whether it caused actual data loss.

title: Remove overdue `legacy-partial-output-inputs` code (TODO targeted v18)
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

compiler

### Description

There are 7 `TODO(legacy-partial-output-inputs): Remove in v18` comments across the compiler, core, and compiler-cli packages. Angular is well past v18 now, and this legacy code is dead weight.

The legacy format allowed directive inputs in partial compilation output to be represented as plain strings or `[publicName, className, transformFn?]` tuples. Since v17.1, a structured object format (`{ classPropertyName, publicName, isSignal, isRequired, transformFunction }`) replaced it. The old paths were kept temporarily for backward compat with older linkers but are no longer needed.

### Affected files

Compiler

### Is this a regression?

No

## Summary

The patch for CVE-2026-22610 / GHSA-jrmj-c5cx-3cw6 added `script|href` and `script|xlink:href` to the `RESOURCE_URL` security context. The fix uses exact string matching throughout the pipeline — both in the compiler's `SECURITY_SCHEMA` lookup and in the runtime's `getUrlSanitizer()`. This creates two gaps:

1. **Namespace prefix bypass**: The schema matches the literal string `xlink:href`. Setting `[attr.s:href]` resolves to the same namespace in the DOM but doesn't match `xlink:href` in the schema, so `securityContext()` returns `NONE`.

2. **Missing SVG elements**: Only `<script>` was added to the schema. Other SVG elements that accept `xlink:href` for resource loading — `<use>`, `<image>`, `<feImage>` — are not in the schema at all. Their `xlink:href` attributes get `SecurityContext.NONE` and bypass sanitization entirely.

title: Scoped Child leave animations
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request? _No response_ ### Description `animate.leave` is strict in that leave animations only happen on the node being removed. No animations are triggered for elements that are children of the node being removed. Many users are confused by this, since it's common to write something like the following: ``` @if (show) {
...
} ``` However this doesn't work, because the `wrapper-for-flexbox` div is the node being removed. It would be nice to have child animations be triggered in this case. However we don't want every child animation under every node to trigger animations. This is too global and results in a queue of child animations firing on any route navigation. We'll want to scope this behavior, likely to the component template. ### Proposed solution As mentioned in the description, have child animations fire scoped within the template of the component being removed, and do not cross component boundaries. ### Alternatives considered Leave the animation behavior as strict as it is.

title: The child element is removed with animation when the parent is removed from the DOM
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?


### Is this a regression?

### Description

When the parent element is removed from the DOM (via `@if` or page navigation), the child elements with `[animate.leave]` directives trigger their animations. According to the Angular documentation, this should not happen - only the element with the animation directive should animate when it is explicitly removed.

title: Make `@defer (on viewport)` configurable via DI
body:
`@defer (on idle)` recently added a DI extension point by introducing an `IdleService` interface and letting apps override it via the `provideIdleServiceWith`. In https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/67262

It would be useful to offer the same for `@defer (on viewport)` by allowing applications to provide a custom viewport observer implementation.

This would make it possible to configure `IntersectionObserverOptions` or use experimental options like [`delay`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Intersection_Observer_API#delay) without requiring major changes to the internals of the framework.

When using `withEventReplay()`, events that make it through to hydrated components (and are handled by them) while the app is not "stable" yet are still replayed when the app becomes stable later. title: Support braced Unicode escapes
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request? compiler ### Description Angular template expressions currently do not support ES6 braced Unicode escapes (e.g. `\u{1F600}`) in string literals. {{ '\u{1F600}' }}

Legacy `\uXXXX` escapes should remain supported for backward compatibility. ### Alternatives considered - Using legacy `\uXXXX` escapes with surrogate pairs for non-BMP characters (e.g., emoji). This is error-prone and less readable, requiring manual calculation and two code units per character. - Avoiding Unicode escapes and directly pasting Unicode characters. This is not always practical for code points outside BMP or for code generation scenarios.

title: @angular/core/primitives/di export collision with @angular/core breaks SystemJS bundling
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

core

### Is this a regression?

Yes

### Description

#### Problem
When bundling Angular 20+ for SystemJS (required for micro-frontends), the `inject` export from `@angular/core/primitives/di` collides with the public `inject` `export from @angular/core`. This causes bundlers to silently drop one of the exports, breaking runtime behavior.

Use case: Micro-frontends using SystemJS for module loading
Angular version: 20+ (affects all versions with `primitives/di`)
Bundler: Rollup (same issue likely affects Webpack with SystemJS output)

Starting in Angular 20, the `fesm2022/` output includes chunked ESM with shared internal modules extracted into separate files. When creating a merged SystemJS bundle that includes both `@angular/core` and its sub-paths, Rollup encounters:

export * from '@angular/core/primitives/di';
```
Both modules export a function named `inject`, causing an ambiguous export conflict. Rollup silently drops one of them during the merge, resulting in missing exports in the final SystemJS output.

While I've found a workaround, other teams using micro-frontends and shared SystemJS bundles are struggling to resolve this. The issue creates real blockers for legitimate architectural patterns in the Angular ecosystem.

### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

compiler-cli, compiler, core, upgrade

### Description

We are an enterprise team migrating an internal SDK from Angular 17 to v20. Due to architectural constraints, we use Full Compilation Mode. We have observed significant shifts in internal instructions (ɵɵpropertyInterpolate1 → ɵɵproperty composition) and token renames (ɵPendingTasks → PendingTasks).

Backward compatibility is broken for our legacy application modules because the v20 runtime does not recognize the v17 ABI. While we understand these are private APIs not subject to backward compatibility constraints, at our scale, we need visibility into these changes to build compatibility shims.

### Proposed solution

Does the team have a generated "diff" of compiler instructions, or is there a recommended way to audit these changes using the Angular Linker’s internal mapping logic? Or a changelog containing such changes which could be publicly shared?

### Alternatives considered

Auditing the @angular/compiler-cli source code to see how the Linker maps declarations to instructions. But this requires deep expertise in the Angular Compiler's internal AST transformations. A public-facing changelog or mapping table would be a much more efficient 'source of truth' for the community and enterprise users than reverse-engineering the Linker logic.

title: Default signal value on initialization
body:

### Description

Currently when we declare a signal property we initialize it with the value of that type. For example:
```
readonly num = signal(0)
``` 

This works well for scenarios where the type is primitive and we know the initial / default value in advance.

It becomes a little bit ugly when it comes to complex types:
```

readonly user = signal<User>({...})

title: Signal Forms allow diferent numeric input methods
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

_No response_

### Description

Currently when your `formField` data is a number the input must be of type number.
Consider this form:
```
readonly data = signal({ age: 4})
readonly f = form(this.data)
```
And this form
```html
<input type="number" [formField]="f.age">
<input type="number" [formField]="f.age" pattern="[0-9]*">
<input type="text" [formField]="f.age" inputmode="number" pattern="[0-9]*"  >
```

This gives several problems. 

1. For one patterns are not allowed. This is according the W3C spec, but some mobile systems (IOS) allow to show the numeric keyboard when you put the pattern="[0-9]*" on a number input.
2. For real good accessibility/mobile support `<input type="text" inputmode="number">` is preferred, but because the 
type is text, it is not allowed. The problems that are solved by this kind of input are explained very well on this site: https://technology.blog.gov.uk/2020/02/24/why-the-gov-uk-design-system-team-changed-the-input-type-for-numbers/ 




### Proposed solution

Allow <input type="text inputmode="number"> for form fields of the numerical type and support the pattern="[0-9]*"

## Summary

This PR upgrades the VS Code Language Server Protocol library from v7.0.0 (LSP 3.16) to v9.0.1 (LSP 3.17).

## Motivation

LSP 3.17 introduces several new features that would benefit Angular developers:
- **Inlay Hints** - Show inline type hints for template variables, pipe outputs, etc.
- **Type Hierarchy** - Navigate class/interface inheritance
- **Inline Values** - Show variable values during debugging

This upgrade is a prerequisite for implementing these features.

## Changes

### Package Updates
| Package | From | To |
|---------|------|-----|
| vscode-languageserver | 7.0.0 | 9.0.1 |
| vscode-languageclient | 7.0.0 | 9.0.1 |
| vscode-languageserver-protocol | 3.16.0 | 3.17.5 |
| vscode-jsonrpc | 6.0.0 | 8.2.0 |

### Breaking Changes Addressed
- `LanguageClient.start()` now returns `Promise<void>` instead of `Disposable`
- `LanguageClient.onReady()` removed - use `await start()` directly
- `protocol2CodeConverter` methods now return Promises (`asWorkspaceEdit`, `asRanges`)
- `SignatureHelp.activeParameter`: `null` → `undefined`

### VS Code Compatibility
Minimum VS Code version: 1.74.3 (already our current minimum)

## Testing
- [x] Unit tests pass (4/4)
- [x] LSP integration tests pass (36 specs)
- [x] Extension packages successfully
- [x] Manual testing in VS Code Extension Host

## Follow-up
This upgrade enables but does not implement the new LSP 3.17 features. Implementation will follow in separate PRs.

title: [signal forms]: debounceForDuration does not resolve its Promise on abort, causing pending awaits
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

forms

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

The current implementation of debounceForDuration does not resolve or reject the returned Promise when the associated AbortSignal is aborted ([source](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/5d46554e3fe8b64c5fefc7a8ce891c179741977e/packages/forms/signals/src/api/rules/debounce.ts#L44)).

This can lead to:
- async execution paths that never complete
- retention of async stack frames and captured variables
- potentially increased memory usage in long-running or frequently triggered scenarios

title: Angular packages are not published in valid Angular Package Format
body:
### Is this a regression?

Yes

### Description

[Angular Package Format](https://angular.dev/tools/libraries/angular-package-format#fesm) defines FESM as "Short for Flattened ES Modules and consists of a file format created by flattening all ES Modules accessible from an entry point into a single ES Module."

Angular currently publishes its packages within an `fesm2022` directory, but the modules are not flattened: the entry points import from other files internal to the package.

This appears to have been broken with Angular 19.

I suspect this is the new-normal, in which case I will find a way to re-bundle them during the linking step so that our build system doesn't choke.
If so, the docs for the APF should be updated, and the files should be moved out of the `fesm2022` directory.

title: Signal forms debounce with additional non-debounced value
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

forms

### Description

Imagine an scenario where a search input has a magnifying glass icon on top of the input (when the input is empty) so the user knows that is a search field. Then the magnifying glass icon should disappear as soon as the user starts typing. However that same field input, using signal forms new api, is implementing a `debounce` to delay the api calls tied to the search input.

The problem with the above is that because of the use of `debounce`, the magnifying glass will not disappear the moment the user starts typing, as the display of the magnifying glass is tied to the form signal as well.

### Proposed solution

The FieldState should expose a non-debounced signal of the value, maybe via the metadata or an additional method.

### Description

When using rune mode in a `.svelte` or `.svelte.ts` file, the `!==`
binary operator is incorrectly compiled so that the resulting
`$.strict_equals()` call receives the wrong `equal` flag, silently
inverting the comparison. This affects **every** `!==` used inside
rune-mode `.svelte` and `.svelte.ts` files, with no warning at compile
time or runtime.

In our codebase, this bug has bitten us at least **38 times** across
**16 files** after a full sweep of all 167 `!==` usages. Every one

  let a = 'hello';
  let b = 'world';
  console.log('a !== b:', a !== b);
</script>

title: Compiler drops parentheses in boolean expressions, changing operator precedence
body:
### Describe the bug

## Description
The Svelte 5 compiler strips parentheses from boolean expressions, 
changing operator precedence and producing incorrect runtime behaviour.



### Reproduction

## Reproduction

Source:
```js
if (hasAlarms && (hasNotBeenRaised || canReRaise)) {
```

Compiled output:
```js
if (hasAlarms && hasNotBeenRaised || canReRaise) {
```

Which evaluates as:
```js
if ((hasAlarms && hasNotBeenRaised) || canReRaise) {
```

## Expected
Compiled output should preserve the original operator precedence.

## Workaround
Split into separate variables to avoid nested boolean expressions:
```js
const canShow = hasNotBeenRaised || canReRaise
const shouldShow = hasAlarms && canShow
if (shouldShow) {
```

title: Async derived rejection escapes inner boundary
body:
### Describe the bug


Looks like this was introduced in 5.55.6.

Used claude for the research/repro:

When an async $derived rejects inside a <svelte:boundary> that handles the error (via failed and/or onerror), the error is delivered twice. The first delivery is handled correctly — the boundary tears down its main effect and renders the failed snippet. But a follow-up settle then re-runs the reaction (finish in reactivity/async.js), which synchronously re-throws the rejected value and routes it through invoke_error_boundary(error, parent). By then the handling boundary's effect has been destroyed, so effect.b is null, and invoke_error_boundary crashes at:

```
// packages/svelte/src/internal/client/error-handling.js
/** @type {Boundary} */ (effect.b).error(error); // effect.b is null
```

with TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'error'). That secondary error has no live boundary to catch it, so it escapes to the parent boundary — i.e. a child component's localized error takes down a much larger part of the tree.

A dependent $derived that reads the awaited value (const model = $derived({ title: data.title })) is what triggers the re-run; without the second read the reaction has nothing to re-evaluate.

title: Compiler drops precedence-significant parentheses in logical expressions (`a && (b || c)` → `a && b || c`)
body:
### Describe the bug

When the Svelte compiler re-prints a JavaScript logical expression that contains a
**parenthesized `||` (or `&&`) nested on the side that needs the parentheses**, it
emits the expression **without the parentheses**. Because `&&` binds tighter than
`||`, this silently changes the runtime semantics of the code.

Source:

```js
if (e.key === 'b' && (e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey)) { ... }
```

Compiled output:

```js
if (e.key === 'b' && e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) { ... }
// JS parses this as: ((e.key === 'b' && e.metaKey) || e.ctrlKey)
```

So the guard fires whenever `e.ctrlKey` is true, regardless of `e.key`. In our app
this made a `Ctrl+B` sidebar shortcut toggle on _any_ Ctrl-held key (and on Ctrl
alone), which the source code clearly does not express.

This affects both `compile` (component markup/script) and `compileModule`
(`.svelte.js` / `.svelte.ts`), so it appears to be in the shared code printer
(esrap), not the template transform.

### Cases

| Source                  | Compiled output       | Semantics                       |
| ----------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `a && (b \|\| c)`       | `a && b \|\| c`       | ❌ changed → `(a && b) \|\| c`  |

| `a === b && (c \|\| d)` | `a === b && c \|\| d` | ❌ changed (real-world case)    |

### Describe the bug

5.56.1 has a codegen bug where parentheses that matter for operator
precedence get dropped. A parenthesized `||` sitting inside an `&&` comes out

meaning:

```
a && (b || c)   →   a && b || c   →   (a && b) || c

	let a = $state(true);
	let b = $state(true);
	let c = $state(true);
	const r = $derived(a && (b || c));
</script>
{r}
`;

title: Docs: clarify that bare `{const}` is not reactive, unlike the `{@const}` it replaces
body:
### Describe the bug

The [declaration-tags docs](https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/declaration-tags) say `{@const ...}` is legacy and to use `{const ...}` instead, but don't mention that the two behave differently. `{@const x = e}` was reactive — a `$derived` behind the
scenes, the same way `{count}` updates in the template. A bare `{const x = e}` is not: it behaves like a `const` in `<script>`, evaluated once. So a `{@const}` → `{const}` rename silently drops reactivity — no compile or type error, the UI just stops updating — until it's rewritten as `{const x = $derived(e)}`.

The page never says this, and its only bare-`{const}` example is inside an `{#each}`. A bare `{const}` there is one-time too — recomputed when an item is created, not when an item's data mutates — but the example's array is static, so it can never go stale, which makes bare `{const}` look reactive when it isn't.

A short note next to "use declaration tags instead" would cover it:

| was              | reactive equivalent       | one-time        |
| ---------------- | ------------------------- | --------------- |
| `{@const x = e}` | `{const x = $derived(e)}` | `{const x = e}` |

title: `set_attributes` doesn't prioritize `type` before `value` for input elements, causing newline stripping with spreads
body:
### Describe the bug

When spreading props onto an `<input>` element and explicitly setting `type="hidden"` after the spread, newlines in the `value` are silently stripped on initial client-side render.

Minimal case:

```svelte
<script>
  const spread = $state({ name: "field", value: "line1\nline2\nline3" });
</script>

<!-- BUG: newlines stripped -->
<input {...spread} type="hidden" />

<!-- OK: newlines preserved -->
<input type="hidden" {...spread} />
```

### Root cause

`set_attributes()` in `src/internal/client/dom/elements/attributes.js` iterates the merged props object with `for (const key in next)`. JavaScript iterates object keys in insertion order, so for:

```js
{ ...spread(), type: "hidden" }
```

`value` (from the spread) is visited **before** `type`. At that point the element is still `type="text"` (the default). Setting `.value` on a text input triggers the [HTML value sanitization algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#value-sanitization-algorithm), which strips `\n` and `\r`. By the time `type` is set to `"hidden"`, the newlines are permanently lost.

The reverse order (`{ type: "hidden", ...spread() }`) works because `type` appears first in insertion order and is set before `value`.

title: SSR compiler does not unwrap $derived thunk for dynamic components with member expressions
body:
### Describe the bug

In SSR mode, when a dynamic component is rendered via a member expression (<a.b.c />) where a is a $derived, the compiler outputs a.b.c directly instead of a().b.c. Since server-side $derived returns a thunk (function) after [#17674](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/pull/17674), a.b is undefined and accessing a.b.c throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'c').

The client compiler handles this correctly by emitting $.get(a).b.c.

**Workaround**

Capture each access in its own $derived:

```
<script>
  const platformIcons = $derived(icons);
  const Icon = $derived(platformIcons.currency.Icon);
</script>
<Icon />
```

That generates $.derived(() => platformIcons().currency.Icon), which works.

https://svelte.dev/playground/2fa2e050cfa44e94a3141dca53ce4ac2?version=latest

<script>

title: Svelte CSS parser fails on apostrophe in CSS block comment with Unexpected end of input
body:
### Describe the bug

In a `.svelte` component `<style>` block, a CSS block comment containing an apostrophe (`'`) can break Svelte’s CSS parsing and produce:

`Unexpected end of input`

The error is reported at the end of the style block (`</style>`), even though CSS braces/parens are balanced.

This is **not** a general comment issue: single-line and multi-line CSS comments parse fine unless they include this apostrophe case.

### Expected behavior

Apostrophes inside CSS block comments should be treated as plain comment text and never affect parsing.

### Actual behavior

Svelte reports:

`Unexpected end of input`

at the end of the `<style>` block.



### Reproduction

### Minimal reproduction

```svelte
<style>
	.foo {
		left: min(
			calc(1px),
			/* across rows (so the marker ends at row 1's right edge). Disabled */
			calc(2px)
		);
	}
</style>
```

If I change `1's` to `1s` (remove apostrophe), parsing succeeds.

### System Info

```shell
- Svelte: `5.53.12`
- `svelte-check`: `4.4.5`
- `@sveltejs/kit`: `2.55.0`
- Node: `v22.17.1`
- npm: `11.6.2`
- OS: macOS (Darwin `25.4.0`)

```

### Additional context

- Both single-line and multi-line CSS comments work in this file.
- The failure is tied to the apostrophe character in comment content (e.g. `1's`).
- Error location points to style EOF, not the comment line.

title: Prop defaults from `$props()` are not reactive to changes in referenced `$state`
body:
### Describe the bug

Prop defaults defined with `$props()` destructuring are not reactive to changes in the reactive values they reference. The fallback is evaluated once (with `untrack()`) and cached — subsequent changes to the underlying `$state` are never reflected.

This affects any pattern where a prop default calls a reactive function:

```svelte
<script>
  import { getTranslation } from './translations.svelte.js';
  let { label = getTranslation('greeting') } = $props();
</script>
```

If `getTranslation('greeting')` returns `"Hello"` at mount time and later changes to `"Hola"`, the component will always display `"Hello"`.

### Root cause

In the compiled output, `$props()` destructuring with a default becomes:

```js
label = $.prop($$props, 'label', 19, () => getTranslation('greeting'))
```

Flag `19` includes `PROPS_IS_LAZY_INITIAL` (16). Inside `$.prop`, the fallback function is evaluated with `untrack()` and cached via a `fallback_dirty` flag that is only reset when the prop is explicitly provided and then removed — not when the reactive dependencies of the fallback change.

### Reproduction

https://svelte.dev/playground/23fb040dbc894601979d7e6e8dc8d633

The reproduction has 3 cases:

1. **Direct template usage** — `{getTranslation('greeting')}` in template markup → **updates correctly** ✅
2. **Prop default on eagerly rendered component** — `let { label = getTranslation('greeting') } = $props()` on a component that mounts before the state changes → **stays stale**... [TRUNCATED]

title: SvelteMap.clear() skips its reactive signal when the map's size is already 0
body:
### Describe the bug

SvelteMap.clear() skips its reactive signal when the map's size is already 0. This means any $derived or $effect that depends on the map will not re-run, leaving reactive state stale.

This becomes a silent data bug when combined with a non-$state variable that changes in the same batch - there is no other signal to compensate, so the derived is never invalidated.

Expected: map.clear() always emits a reactive signal, regardless of current size — consistent with how $state assignments emit signals even when the new value equals the old one.

Actual: When map.size === 0, clear() is a no-op in the reactive sense. Any $derived/$effect depending on the map is not re-run.

Svelte version: 5.55.0

Note, it doesn't crash and is easy to work around (make the companion variable $state, or add a dummy set+delete after clear()). However, it violates the principle of least surprise — calling .clear() should always be observable to the reactive graph, just as calling $state's setter with the same value still notifies dependents.

title: `{@const}` inside `{#each}` goes stale when prop-derived value is only consumed inside an array callback
body:
### Describe the bug

A `{@const}` inside `{#each}` does not invalidate when its reactive dependency
arrives via a **prop** and that dependency is only referenced inside an array
callback (`.find()`, `.filter()`, `.some()`, etc.) rather than in the outer
expression.

From the template's perspective the prop changed, a sibling `{@const}` that
reads the prop directly updates correctly, but the `{@const}` whose expression
only touches the prop inside a callback closure stays frozen at its previous
value.

## Required conditions

Both must be present:

1. The reactive dependency is a **prop** — does not reproduce when the same
   value is a local variable or a store.
2. That prop value appears **only inside the callback** of the array method —
   removing it from inside and placing it in the outer expression fixes the
   staleness.

No transition, no `{#if}` toggle, no async wrapper needed.

title: $state mutation inside getter read during flush deadlocks scheduler (regression in 5.53.8)
body:
### Describe the bug

A store getter that lazily writes `$state` on first read deadlocks the scheduler when read inside a template binding during the flush/commit phase. The UI freezes permanently — no errors, no stack overflow, no crash.

**Works in:** 5.53.7  
**Broken in:** 5.53.8, 5.53.9  
**Likely cause:** #17805 "simplify scheduling logic"

### Reproduction

https://github.com/vdg/svelte-5.53.8-scheduler-deadlock

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vdg/svelte-5.53.8-scheduler-deadlock
cd svelte-5.53.8-scheduler-deadlock
npm install
npm run dev
```

1. Click **"Open panel"**
2. Click **"Counter"** — counter does not update, UI is frozen
3. No console errors

Change to `svelte@5.53.7` → works fine.

### The pattern

A module store with a getter that writes `$state` on first read:

```js
let panelWidth = $state(null)

export default {
  get panelWidth () {
    if (panelWidth === null) panelWidth = DEFAULT_WIDTH  // writes $state
    return panelWidth
  }
}
```

Read by a template binding:

```svelte
<div style:width={store.panelWidth ? `${store.panelWidth}px` : null}>
```

### What happens

1. User action triggers a flush
2. During commit, the `style:width` binding reads `store.panelWidth` for the first time
3. The getter writes `$state` (lazy init)
4. In 5.53.8+, this stalls the scheduler — no further updates are processed

### Workaround

Avoid writing `$state` inside getters:

```js
get panelWidth () {
  return panelWidth ?? DEFAULT_WIDTH  // no state write
}
```

title: SSR: `$store` inside `<option>` text content is not wrapped with `store_get()`, causing ReferenceError
body:
### Describe the bug

When using a `$store` variable inside the text content of an `<option>` element within a `<select>`, the SSR compiler does not wrap the reference with `store_get()`. This causes a `ReferenceError: $store is not defined` during server-side rendering.

This is a common pattern when using i18n libraries like `sveltekit-i18n`, where `t` is a store containing a translation function.

### Reproduction

```svelte
<script>
	import { readable } from 'svelte/store';

	const t = readable((key: string) => key);

	let value = $state('');
</script>

<select bind:value>
	<option disabled value="">{$t('placeholder')}</option>
	<option value="a">A</option>
	<option value="b">B</option>
</select>
```

When this component is server-side rendered, it throws:

```
ReferenceError: $t is not defined
```

All other template expressions correctly compile `$store` to `store_get($$store_subs ??= {}, "$store", store)(...)`, but the `Renderer.option()` code path outputs raw `$store(...)`.

**Compiled SSR output (incorrect):**

```js
$$renderer.option({ disabled: true }, $t('placeholder'));
```

**Expected SSR output:**

```js
$$renderer.option({ disabled: true }, store_get(($$store_subs ??= {}), '$t', t)('placeholder'));
```

`$store` inside `<option>` text content should be compiled with `store_get()` like all other template expressions, and SSR should render without errors.

title: Scopes aren't tracked correctly in function arguments
body:
### Describe the bug

Svelte's scope tracker reuses the same scope for a function's arguments and body. Body declarations end up referenced in argument initializers shadowing the parent scopes' declarations, potentially making an initializer [skip rune transformation logic](https://svelte.dev/playground/590c171f1436486e9072bbc2641c9b53?version=5.53.3).

~~I tried fixing this a few different ways, but I couldn't find a clean way to deal with this due to my lack of familiarity with the v5 codebase (hi, everyone, miss you!). My thinking was to create two separate scopes, one for arguments and one for the body (either through the body's `BlockStatement` or the `*Function*` themselves), and perhaps call `add_state_transformers` on the function visitors, but every variation I tried ended up interacting badly with different compilation pipeline assumptions.~~

Turns out I just forgot to make the `BlockStatement` scope non-porous as opposed to the function's. Not sure this is the "cleanest" solution, but `BlockStatement` already had special-casing for the function cases. See attached PR.

Scope confusion causes runes' objects to be used instead of its values: https://svelte.dev/playground/590c171f1436486e9072bbc2641c9b53?version=5.53.3

title: `$derived` with `await` delays source `$state` update
body:
### Describe the bug

When you use a state in a `$derived` syntax with `await`, the state update does not trigger a render until the async process completes


### Reproduction

```svelte
<script>
	let count = $state(0); // not updated immediately
	let count2 = $derived(await f(count));

	function f(n) {
		return new Promise((f) => setTimeout(() => f(n), n + 1000));
	}
</script>

<button onclick={() => count += 1}>
	clicks: {count} / {count2}
</button>
```

- Playground: https://svelte.dev/playground/0841bb05b5fa408f883edd59210479f6?version=5.51.0

When the state `count` is update, the template `{count}` is not updated until the derived `count2` update completes

FYI we can use `$effect` to avoid the problem:

```ts
let count = $state(0);
let count2 = $state(0);
$effect(async () => (count2 = await f(count)));

### Describe the bug

**TL;DR**: Using experimental async (`$derived(await ...)`) in a component that also uses `{@attach}` with a function from `bind:this` breaks SSR hydration. In development, this causes a warning. In production build with nested components, the application crashes completely and the page fails to render.

The issue appears to be that the async boundary interacts incorrectly with the `{@attach}` directive during hydration. title: `createContext` behaves differently between client and server
body:
### Describe the bug

While the [client implementation of `createContext`](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/blob/06e6ef83b801a3ca014af4629abad76ac2d35eef/packages/svelte/src/internal/client/context.js#L81) throws `e.missing_context()` if the context hasn't been set, the [server implementation](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/blob/06e6ef83b801a3ca014af4629abad76ac2d35eef/packages/svelte/src/internal/server/context.js#L20) returns the result of of `getContext` directly, so it returns undefined rather than throwing if the context hasn't been set.

This can lead to subtle bugs, for example catching the error to provide a default value works on the client but silently fails on the server. The `get()` type signature is also wrong for server code where undefined can sneak past the types.

I hit this using optional context to manage heading levels. The server rendered different tags than the client, making for a funky heading tree and hydration mismatches.

Making both throw aligns with [documented behaviour](https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/svelte#createContext). But would making a function start throwing count as a breaking change? I'm happy to pitch in with a PR once I know what approach to take.

title: Allow using a timing function as easing
body:
### Describe the problem

If you have a `cubic-bezier()` or `linear()` timing function, which browsers natively support, you can't use it as your Svelte transition's easing. Instead, you have to reimplement what the browser already has so Svelte can pass every time interval through your reimplementation given that it'll be rendered with linear easing.

### Describe the proposed solution

Allow using a string for easing, which will be forwarded to `.animate()`.

(Perhaps even, if [linear() has enough support](https://caniuse.com/?search=linear%28%29), convert existing function easing to a `linear()` timing function? May look slightly different from the current "get exact value every frame" way though)

First, a quick note: the unusual implementation in the REPL is necessary for bind:offsetWidth to work correctly in my use case, though this detail isn’t directly relevant to the issue at hand.

title: Regression: draw transition removes element early after Svelte v5.41.1

### Describe the bug

In Svelte releases from v5.41.1 onward the `draw` transition appears to stop part‑way through its duration and the element is removed from the DOM early. title: Async: Values can get out of sync
body:
### Describe the bug

If you have a value X that causes a pending batch, and while that batch is pending cause creation of another batch which creates a new branch and therefore new template effects which also read that value X, those template effects are not correctly rescheduled once the pending batch resolves. As a result, the shown values of X get out of sync (once shows the old, once the new value). 

I believe it happens because the pending batch does not know of the new effects that are created (they are not in its (maybe_)dirty arrays), therefore does not schedule them as (maybe_)dirty on revival and therefore never runs them.

title: Allow passing custom options to shadow DOM constructor
body:
### Describe the problem

Currently, the only thing you can pass to shadow DOM contructor is either [`mode: "open"`](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/blob/8ebc3b1337bd12931f5608ab608b9668e10aa6c2/packages/svelte/src/internal/client/dom/elements/custom-element.js#L49) or nothing at all.
https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/custom-elements#Component-options

This means that you can't create shadow DOM with `closed` shadow root or change any other options of [`attachShadow()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/attachShadow).



### Describe the proposed solution

Instead of passing only `"none"` to the `shadow` custom element option, allow passing the whole [`options`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/attachShadow#options) object, which would be then passed to `attachShadow()`.

This would allow changing shadow root mode to `closed` and would also allow you to customize all the other options.

This would probably be considered a breaking change for everyone already using `shadow: "none"`, so you should be able to still pass either:
- `shadow: "none"` or `shadow: "open"` - to maintain backwards compatibility
- something like `shadow: { mode: 'closed', clonable: false }` (or any other options)

### Importance

nice to have

title: Server `render()` result shape is impractical to work with
body:
### Describe the bug

When awaiting `render()` when `compilerOptions.experimental.async` isn't enabled, the `experimental_async_ssr` warning is shown. Problem is, there's no way to know if the result is awaitable from its shape because `then` is always present: https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/blob/main/packages/svelte/src/internal/server/renderer.js#L352-L384. That's an issue for us in Astro.

My recommendation would be to only set the `then` property if `async_mode_flag` is true so we can do checks like `'then' in result`:

```js
let result = render(...)
if (isPromise(result)) {
  result = await result
}
```

That currently forces us to make a pretty big workaround, see https://github.com/withastro/astro/pull/14526.

I'd be happy to open a PR

title: `:this` CSS pseudoclass for selecting the component itself
body:
### Describe the problem In Svelte we can use `:global` inside scoped styles to create CSS selectors that influence child components and elements: ```ts
{@render children()}
``` This is wonderful, but demands that we specify an element in the component as a selector. However sometimes we would like to create a deep selector without a surrounding element. When using headless UI libraries like [Bits UI](https://www.bits-ui.com/), its natural to create wrapper components. In such wrappers, I'd like to select child elements from the library, _without_ selecting anything _outside_ the component. But I would _also_ like to avoid adding superfluous wrapper elements around them. I could pass a class into the component to narrow the selector; however, this relies on the fact the library offers a prop for this, which may not always be the case. To make things worse, I can still accidentally repeat the selector elsewhere if I happen to pass the same class again. title: `$props.id()` output format clashes with Server Side Include format
body:
### Describe the bug

When [SSIs](https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_ssi_module.html#commands) are turned on in Nginx the server tries to parse `<!--#text-->` -- which is the same [format output](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Asveltejs/svelte%20%27%3C!--%23%27&type=code) during SSR when `$props.id()` is used. Nginx can't parse this and the default is to print `[an error occurred while processing the directive]` in the html (replacing Svelte's hydration comment `<!--#s1-->`)

Would it be possible to change the format of the `props_id()` renderer output? Maybe like `<!--$`? That seems safe in the [corresponding props_id hydration code too](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/blob/main/packages/svelte/src/internal/client/dom/template.js)?

title: Feature Request:  Built-in access of a $derived's current value
body:
### Describe the problem

Imagine a scenario where one would like to stop cascading a change through a chain of $derived values.

```plaintext
$state change -> $derived A changes -> $derived B changes -> $derived C changes -> $effects
```

Imagine that `$derived A` has decided that, despite the change, it is not useful for the downstream calculations to run, perhaps because the original state change will imply that, for example, something gets reset, making the calculation effort of all downstream values, a waste of time.

If I understand Svelte, if the reported new value of `$derived A` is the same as its previous value, the downstream chain is not going to be activated.  That would be the goal.

Now imagine that for whatever reason, `$derived A` is interested in **not** performing its calculations.  Perhaps calculating will produce a different value, and we want to **force** the previous one.  What then?

### Describe the proposed solution

It would be ideal if we could short-circuit calculations of a `$derived` by simply using the previous signal value:

```typescript
let someDerived = $derived.by(() => {
  if (<some condition>) {
    return $derived.previous(); // Or current?
  }
  ...
});

let someDerived = $derived(<some condition> ? $derived.previous() : ...);
```

The alternative I see is to manually track the previous value in user land.  I dislike this approach because that value is already stored somewhere.  I want to access that copy. 😄   If you please.

title: `push` array is not proxied when array is optional
body:
### Describe the bug

Hi, I found an issue that might be expected behavior but it's odd as you can make it work by mutating unrelated state

When using the rune $state inside a class to expose a prop, `myClass.prop` it behaves as expected, it also behaves correctly when nesting it inside a sub property that is itself another class `myClass.childClass.prop`

title: Remote form().for() shares instance cache between forms during SSR
body:
### Describe the bug

Remote `form()` functions return the same instance from their `for()` methods when not client-side rendering. All forms using the same key will initially use the form action for the first form to use the key.

The expected behavior is that each form function has its own instance cache (so for example, an `updatePost` and `deletePost` form could each refer to the same `post.id`). This is how `for()` seems to behave during CSR, but *not* during SSR, which affects environments where CSR or JavaScript are disabled.

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/sveltejs-kit-template-default-qfi3gy8i

Inspecting the second form element reveals that it has the same `action` as the first form. Changing the value of `csr` in `+page.js` and refreshing corrects this.

I would like to respectfully open a discussion regarding the possibility of moving the compiler and internal codebase back to TypeScript. I fully appreciate the rationale behind the initial decision to use JavaScript with JSDoc annotations, as articulated by Rich Harris: “We also eliminate an entire class of annoying papercuts that will be familiar to anyone who has worked with the uneven landscape of TypeScript tooling” ([reddit.com](https://www.reddit.com/r/programming/comments/13f9mdx/typescript_is_not_worth_it_for_developing/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)). The concerns about tooling friction, dual compilation, and iteration speed were entirely valid at the time.

However, the development landscape has evolved significantly. Node 23.6 now allows TypeScript files to run natively, substantially reducing the historical overhead of compilation. Tooling has also improved, with solutions such as tsx providing near-instant feedback loops. Many of the previous bottlenecks around compile-then-run workflows are now largely obsolete.

At the same time, the developer ecosystem has shifted. More contributors today are TypeScript-native rather than relying on JavaScript with TypeScript adaptations. Reintroducing TypeScript internally could broaden the pool of potential maintainers, reduce onboarding friction, and enable the team to take advantage of modern TypeScript features and stricter typing guarantees without compromising speed or simplicity.

title: Hash styles by filename rather than contents
body:
### Describe the problem

Svelte adds `svelte-xyz123` hashes to CSS rules and the corresponding elements, so that styles don't affect other components. This hash is based on the contents of the `<style>` block.

This works but it means that the hashes [change frequently between deployments](https://bsky.app/profile/uncenter.dev/post/3lwlrsfjmo22l). It might be better to default to hashing based on the filename instead. I think the reason we didn't originally do this was that not all project setups made the filename available to the compiler, but now that most people are using `vite-plugin-svelte` that's probably not an issue any more.

### Describe the proposed solution

Update this...

https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/blob/7b2d7746277dae6372ed7b836ad895bde536dc89/packages/svelte/src/compiler/validate-options.js#L73-L75

...to this:

```js
cssHash: fun(({ css, filename, hash }) => {
  return `svelte-${hash(filename ?? css)}`;
}),
```

### Importance

nice to have

title: Support for arbitrary :bind expressions
body:
### Describe the problem

If you try to use a function or anything other than a simple identifier or a member expression in a `bind:` directive you get an error:

```
<input bind:value={foo().bar} />
```

```
Can only bind to an Identifier or MemberExpression or a `{get, set}` pair
```

Since svelte 5.9.0 it is possible to do the above using get/set [function bindings](https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/bind#Function-bindings) like this:

```
<input bind:value={
    () => foo().bar,
    (v) => foo().bar = v
} />
```

For cases like this where you're just getting/setting the same property on some arbitrary expression, it would make sense to be able to use the default `bind:` syntax as a shortcut.

### Describe the proposed solution

Arbitrary bind expressions like this:

```
<input bind:value={foo().bar} />
```

Should compile into get/set bindings like this:

```
<input bind:value={
    () => foo().bar,
    (v) => foo().bar = v
} />
```

The only constraint is that the expression be a property access of some kind, but the expression for the object and the expression for the property can both be arbitrary expressions.

In other words, these would all be valid:

```
<input bind:value={foo().bar} />
<input bind:value={foo[bar]} />
<input bind:value={foo[bar()]} />
<input bind:value={foo()[bar()]} />
```

But these would still result in an error:

```
<input bind:value={foo()} />
<input bind:value={foo.bar()} />
```

### Importance

nice to have

title: Getting remote functions waterfall despite following the docs
body:
### Describe the bug

This is what the [docs for `await_waterfall` warning](https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/runtime-warnings#Client-warnings-await_waterfall) recommend to do to avoid waterfalls:

```js
let aPromise = $derived(one());
let bPromise = $derived(two());

let a = $derived(await aPromise);
let b = $derived(await bPromise);
```

And this is what I'm doing:

```js
let quotesPromise = $derived(getQuotes());
