When Python code converts Unicode strings to bytes using `ord() & 0xFF` or `encode('latin-1')`, high bits are silently discarded:

When an endpoint uses both dependency-injected `BackgroundTasks` and returns a `Response` object that already has its own `background` attribute set, the injected background tasks are silently discarded. title: Support for propertyNames in OpenAPI schema when using dict[Enum, ...] with Pydantic v2
body:
When using dict[StrEnum, ...] or RootModel[dict[StrEnum, ...]] in a FastAPI app with Pydantic v2, the generated OpenAPI schema does not enumerate the enum values used as dictionary keys. Instead, the UI shows [any-key], which does not reflect the actual constraints.

As of Pydantic v2.11+, support for emitting propertyNames with enum constraints was added via [PR #10478](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/10478). This allows OpenAPI/JSON Schema to correctly express restrictions on object keys, such as:

```
{
  "type": "object",
  "propertyNames": {
    "type": "string",
    "enum": ["foo", "bar"]
  },
  "additionalProperties": {
    "type": "integer"
  }
}
```

However, FastAPI currently does not appear to consume or propagate the propertyNames node from Pydantic’s schema output, so these constraints are missing in the OpenAPI spec and Swagger UI.

### Expected Behavior

FastAPI should correctly include propertyNames in the generated OpenAPI schema when dict[Enum, T] is used as a request/response model with Pydantic v2. This would allow Swagger UI to better reflect the allowed dictionary keys.

### To Reproduce
```
from enum import StrEnum
from pydantic import RootModel
from fastapi import FastAPI

class MyEnum(StrEnum):

    bar = "bar"

class MyModel(RootModel[dict[MyEnum, int]]):
    pass

app = FastAPI()

@app.post("/test")
def test_endpoint(model: MyModel):
    return model
```

title: Basic auth `realm` is REQUIRED but handled as optional
body:
According to https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7617#autoid-3 , specification of the `realm` parameter is REQUIRED, so making `realm` optional here

https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/643d2845de09a437b955a163ab25eb0887bfd0e1/fastapi/security/http.py#L195

and at related places, is misleading and makes it easy to create non-conforming APIs. It bit me when a Shelly device refused (rightfully) to authenticate against the API which was using the default (missing) `realm` behavior.

title: Update docs include syntax for source examples
body:
### Privileged issue

- [X] I'm @tiangolo or he asked me directly to create an issue here.

### Issue Content

This is a good first contribution. :nerd_face: 

The code examples shown in the docs are actual Python files. They are even tested in CI, that's why you can always copy paste an example and it will always work, the example is tested.

The way those examples are included in the docs used a specific format. But now there's a new format available that is much simpler and easier to use than the previous one, in particular in complex cases, for example when there are examples in multiple versions of Python.

But not all the docs have the new format yet. The docs should use the new format to include examples. That is the task. :nerd_face: 

**It should be done as one PR per page updated.**

## Simple Example

Before, the format was like:

````markdown
```Python hl_lines="3"
{!../../docs_src/first_steps/tutorial001.py!}
```
````

Now the new format looks like:

````markdown
{* ../../docs_src/first_steps/tutorial001.py hl[3] *}
````

* Instead of `{!` and `!}` it uses `{*` and `*}`
* It no longer has a line above with:

````markdown
```Python
````

* And it no longer has a line below with:

````markdown
```
````

* The highlight is no longer a line with e.g. `hl_lines="3"` (to highlight line 3), but instead in the same line there's a `hl[3]`.

FastAPI does not validate custom string build using `Annotated[str, StringConstraints(...)]`

**Temporary solution**
_My solution is to annotate the constrained type with Path again, then it seems to work:_

```python
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import FastAPI, Path
from pydantic import StringConstraints

# In my case this is imported from a lib with pydantic but without fastapi,
# so it can't be changed to Annotated[str, Path(pattern=r"^[a-fA-F0-9]+$")]
Identifier = Annotated[str, StringConstraints(pattern=r"^[a-fA-F0-9]+$")]


app = FastAPI()


@app.get("/{some_id}")
async def get_something(some_id: Annotated[Identifier, Path()]):
    return some_id

```

**Feature request**
Would be nice if fastapi would be able to get the constraint directly from the `Identifier` type without being required to add `Annotated[Identifier, Path()]`.

The problem is that a "valid JSON Schema" includes a `bool` (i.e. `true` and `false`).

title: Why does APIRouter not allow extra keyword args to be passed along to a route class?
body:
How come there is no way to pass any extra data down through the route decorators to a custom route class.

This seems like a small addition for what could be a very useful feature? Is there a reason this has not been done.

```
@router.get("/", some_extra_info = 1)
def get_something(): ...
```

Storing this in, say, a `route_extra` dict would allow you to do something like

`if router.routes[0].route_extra.get("some_extra_info") == 1: ...`

The only way to do this currently is to duplicate (since these classes are rather inextensible by nature) `APIRouter` and `APIRoute`.

The change would be rather trivial, of only adding a **kwds parameter to each of the decorators and appropriate methods, and add to the APIRoute class a new public property called extra_data which receives this.

from starlette.requests import Request
from starlette.responses import StreamingResponse
from starlette.background import BackgroundTask

import httpx

client = httpx.AsyncClient(base_url="http://containername:7800/")


async def _reverse_proxy(request: Request):
    url = httpx.URL(path=request.url.path, query=request.url.query.encode("utf-8"))
    rp_req = client.build_request(
        request.method, url, headers=request.headers.raw, content=await request.body()
    )
    rp_resp = await client.send(rp_req, stream=True)
    return StreamingResponse(
        rp_resp.aiter_raw(),
        status_code=rp_resp.status_code,
        headers=rp_resp.headers,
        background=BackgroundTask(rp_resp.aclose),
    )


app.add_route("/titles/{path:path}", _reverse_proxy, ["GET", "POST"])
```

title: An application that depends on spring-boot-security-oauth2-resource-server may fail to start with a ClassNotFoundException when Reactor is on the classpath but WebFlux is not
body:
Spring Boot `4.1.0` conditions to apply `ReactiveOAuth2ResourceServerAutoConfiguration` have changed, making it possible to try to instantiate a `SpringReactiveOpaqueTokenIntrospector`, even if WebFlux dependencies are not on the classpath.

In my case, this results in `java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: org.springframework.web.reactive.function.BodyInserter`.

The following tests for tiny WebMvc applications with introspection properties crash:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/ch4mpy/spring-addons.git
cd spring-addons
git checkout boot-4.1.0
mvn test
```

#### Thoughts
Conditions for Boot to auto-configure beans should be quite conservative. In the case of an opaque token introspector, this should happen only if:
- introspection properties are present
- the required security dependencies are on the classpath
- there is no opaque token introspector provided by the application (`@ConditionalOnMissingBean`). 

Additionally, depending on what is on the classpath, at most one of the reactive or synchronized implementations should be instantiated.

title: PropertiesWebClientHttpServiceGroupConfigurer has highest precedence, preventing other configurers from being ordered ahead of it
body:
`PropertiesWebClientHttpServiceGroupConfigurer#getOrder()` still returns `Ordered.HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE`, while the RestClient sibling was changed to `Ordered.HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE + 10` in 72eaeecd5cd for gh-48296.

This leaves WebClient-backed HTTP service groups with the limitation that gh-48296 fixed for RestClient. A `WebClientHttpServiceGroupConfigurer` ordered at, say, `Ordered.HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE + 5` cannot supply an initial `WebClient.Builder` through `InitializingClientCallback`. The properties configurer runs first, creates the default builder through the `ClientCallback` variant of `forEachClient`, and the initializing callback then fails with "Client builder already initialized".

If this is considered a bug, would it be okay for me to submit a small PR?

title: High number of connections due to mongo health indicator
body:
Hello,

we noticed a high number of connections created by our microservices after migrating to Spring Boot 4.0.6.\
We have about 80 microservices in our product and they used to create around 200 connections to MongoDB.\
After migrating to Spring Boot 4, we noticed that microservices were creating around 1300 connections.

After analysis, we identified the mongo health indicator as the root cause of this issue, more precisely the refactoring done with #47051.

Our context:
- every microservice has its own database
- our microservices use the reactive mongo health indicator to check database connectivity
- all microservices in a Kubernetes namespace use the same MongoDB user (to avoid limitation in MongoDB Atlas)

With Spring Boot 3, the mongo health indicator was running a single HELLO command in the database of the microservice.

Since Spring Boot 4, the reactive indicator runs a HELLO command on all databases of the namespace (around 80) and it does so in parallel for the reactive health indicator (due to usage of flatMap).

To fix the issue, we overwrote the mongo health indicator to only check the current database.

Would you consider reverting mongo indicators (blocking & reactive) to their previous implementation (using mongoTemplate & reactiveMongoTemplate) ?

Some of these libraries have auto configuration beans that are referenced in the file `META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports` of the library. In the springboot applications we develop, we often specify `com.maycompany` as the value for `scanBasePackages`. This way we automatically get all the beans from all our libraries.

title: Support MVC controller role on @Bean definitions
body:
**Problem**

Spring MVC registers @RequestMapping handlers for beans whose type is detected as a controller component, typically via @Controller or @RestController.

Beans created via @Configuration / @Bean are not considered MVC handler candidates unless the implementation class itself carries the controller annotation.

This couples:

* bean lifecycle definition (@Configuration, @Bean)
* with MVC role definition (@Controller / @RestController)

**Use case**

In feature-flagged applications, a spring bean or even a controller can be defined as bean conditionally exposed via configuration:

```
@Configuration
@ConditionalOnProperty(name = "features.user.enabled", havingValue = "true")
class UserWebConfiguration {

  @Bean
  UserController userController(UserService service) {
    return new UserController(service);
  }
}
```

**Limitation**

There is currently no supported mechanism to mark a bean created via @Bean as an MVC controller without annotating its implementation class.

As a result, MVC role assignment is strictly tied to class-level metadata rather than bean definition metadata.

**Existing Workarounds**

We can of course:
* annotate the RestController with ConditionalOnProperty
* or disable the package of the rest controller from the scan

But these are workarounds (the point was to be able to use a @Configuration to centralize the mocing parts of the module configuration).

**Relevant links**

* https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/34813#issueco... [TRUNCATED]

title: Remove stale gRPC entry from community starters
body:

This appears to have become stale after [c35b21a](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/commit/c35b21adb40fc7e5a267523fd542f6946f60af94) added Spring Boot gRPC client support. Its parent, [e61bb6d](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/commit/e61bb6df5bedde613e58bdc07c956f60a4d501a7), had already added server support, so Spring Boot now provides official gRPC starters:

- [spring-boot-starter-grpc-client](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/tree/ddb2b8e0eb2b34c8d8152d321c97b1cf63e0f093/starter/spring-boot-starter-grpc-client)
- [spring-boot-starter-grpc-server](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/tree/ddb2b8e0eb2b34c8d8152d321c97b1cf63e0f093/starter/spring-boot-starter-grpc-server)

title: spring-boot:build-image fails on Docker 29.5.1 against Paketo Noble builders due to /var/run symlink (CVE-2026-41568 hardening)
body:
## Summary

After upgrading the Docker daemon to **29.5.1**, `spring-boot:build-image` fails when building against the Paketo `builder-noble-java-tiny`. The same plugin version and the same builder image digest succeed on Docker **29.5.0**.

The boundary aligns with the security fix shipped in Docker 29.5.1 for **CVE-2026-41568 / [GHSA-vp62-88p7-qqf5](https://github.com/moby/moby/security/advisories/GHSA-vp62-88p7-qqf5)**. Per the advisory, the fix uses `os.Root` (Go 1.24+) to scope mount-destination creation during `docker cp` / `PUT /containers/{id}/archive`, refusing to traverse symlinks that escape the container root. The daemon log line we see is consistent with that check rejecting an operation involving `/var/run`, which is a symlink (`/var/run -> /run`) in every Paketo builder we checked. We have not pinpointed the exact commit in 29.5.1 — this is inference from the timing, the advisory text, and the daemon log.

## Versions

- `spring-boot-maven-plugin`: **4.0.6**
- Docker Engine (Server): **29.5.1** (fails), **29.5.0** (works) — verified by downgrading on the same host and re-running an unchanged build.
- Builder: `paketobuildpacks/builder-noble-java-tiny@sha256:c8b5f936e6d9af492af4a493b4a03eaf496fe51f206c5d53ccddab7871ed4ef5` (identical digest in both passing and failing runs).

## What we observe

Maven output on the failing run:

```

  (default-cli) on project app: ... [TRUNCATED]

title: ProcessRunner does not restore interrupt flag on InterruptedException
body:
In `ProcessRunner`, two `InterruptedException` catch blocks do not restore the thread's interrupt flag before re-throwing or returning:

1. `waitForProcess` (line 140): catches `InterruptedException`, throws `IllegalStateException` without calling `Thread.currentThread().interrupt()` first, and without chaining the original exception.
2. `ReaderThread.toString` (line 192): catches `InterruptedException` and returns `""` without restoring the interrupt flag.

This is inconsistent with every other `InterruptedException` handler in the codebase (e.g., `LogbackLoggingSystem`, `SpringApplicationShutdownHook`, `ServiceReadinessChecks`, `FileWatcher`, `OnClassCondition`) which all restore the flag.

Without restoring the flag, code higher in the call stack (such as Docker Compose lifecycle shutdown handling) cannot detect that the thread was interrupted.

title: RabbitProperties enable SSL when `spring.rabbitmq.ssl.bundle` is overridden to an empty string
body:
I believe there is a bug in Spring Boot's RabbitMQ auto-configuration when a configured SSL bundle is overridden to an empty string in a profile-specific configuration.

## Problem

If a base configuration sets a RabbitMQ SSL bundle and a profile-specific configuration tries to disable it with:

```yaml
spring:
  rabbitmq:
    ssl:
      enabled: false
      bundle: ""
```

This is relevant when a default profile uses an SSL bundle for production/stage, and a `local` profile wants to switch RabbitMQ back to plain AMQP on localhost.

Base `application.yml`:

spring:
  rabbitmq:
    host: rabbitmq.ucl.svc.cluster.local
    port: 5671
    ssl:
      enabled: true
      bundle: rabbitmq-ca
```

Profile-specific `application-local.yml`:

```yaml
spring:
  rabbitmq:
    host: localhost
    port: 5672
    ssl:
      enabled: false
      bundle: ""

RabbitMQ SSL is still enabled when the `local` profile is active.

title: MappingsEndpoint reports the context's own ID as parentId when a parent exists
body:
`MappingsEndpoint` sets the `parentId` of `ContextMappingsDescriptor` to the context's own ID when a parent exists, rather than the parent's ID:

```java
return new ContextMappingsDescriptor(mappings,
    (applicationContext.getParent() != null) ? applicationContext.getId() : null);
```

`mappings()` already keys the response map by `target.getId()`, so the descriptor's `parentId` ends up equal to its own map key when a parent is present, which prevents reconstructing the context tree from the response.

The other actuator endpoints with the same `parentId` field use `getParent().getId()`:

- `BeansEndpoint.java:124` — `(parent != null) ? parent.getId() : null`
- `ConfigurationPropertiesReportEndpoint.java:150` — `context.getParent().getId()`
- `ConditionsReportEndpoint.java:124` — `context.getParent().getId()`

A separate parity observation between the two `Dispatcher*MappingDescriptionProvider` classes:

- `DispatcherServletsMappingDescriptionProvider` (webmvc) wraps its static provider list with `Collections.unmodifiableList(...)`.
- `DispatcherHandlersMappingDescriptionProvider` (webflux) uses `Arrays.asList(...)`, which is fixed-size but mutable via `set(i, ...)`.

I can submit a PR for the `parentId` fix if this is accepted. Let me know whether to bundle or skip the `Arrays.asList` alignment.

title: Fetch overall health/info from Actuator in parallel
body:
### Enhancement

Hello.

I was checking the code in Actuator and, for what I can see, it fetches the results of the various health indicators sequentially.
I didn't manage to check the info contributors part, but I would expect there a similar situation.

If would be great if, instead, they would be fetched in parallel, ideally with virtual threads, if enabled.

**Problem**

If some health indicators are slow, their slowness is cumulative for the total time needed for `/health` (or `/health/foo` where `foo` is a group or a composite indicator) to return the result.
This is especially crucial for monitoring systems which need to get data as fast as possible.
By parallelizing them, assuming that enough resources are available, the overall time will be equal to the time of the slowest indicator which will be, by construction, faster (or equal) than before.

**Possible issues: ordering**

Order of the various results may be potentially an issue if it's expected but, maybe, on an high level, it could be possible to:

1. iterate first over the various indicators/contributors in the order they're returned by the registry and attach to them an "index" (e.g.: OrderedHealthIndicator(index) extends HealthIndicator`)
2. execute them in parallel and make each job return the index together with the result (e.g: OrderedHealth(index) extends Health`)
3. sort the results by index and compose the final health

title: ConfigurationPropertiesReportEndpoint exposes AOP proxy internals
body:
### Spring Boot version
4.0.6 (also reproduces with Spring Cloud 2025.1.1 — `spring-cloud-context` provides `@RefreshScope`)

### Description

A `@RefreshScope`-annotated `@ConfigurationProperties` bean is exposed via
`/actuator/configprops` with the AOP proxy's `Advised` interface getters
(`targetSource`, `exposeProxy`, `preFiltered`) included alongside the
legitimate `@ConfigurationProperties` fields.

This happens **independently of `BufferingApplicationStartup`** — the leak
is intrinsic to how the endpoint handles refresh-scoped CGLIB proxies.
With `BufferingApplicationStartup` configured, the leak balloons by orders
of magnitude because the Jackson serializer follows
`targetSource.beanFactory.applicationStartup.bufferedTimeline.events[…]`
into the entire startup-event buffer (hundreds to thousands of entries
per refresh-scoped bean).

The endpoint also exposes the bean **twice** — once as the proxy
(`beanName`) and once as the underlying target (`scopedTarget.beanName`).
The target serializes cleanly; only the proxy variant carries the
`Advised` leak.

The combination `@RefreshScope` + `@ConfigurationProperties` is the
standard Spring Cloud pattern for runtime-reloadable properties, so every
project using this pattern is affected.

### Reproducer

Minimal multi-module reproducer (no security, ~10 files):
https://github.com/ahoehma/springboot-refreshscope-properties-bug

```
mvn -DskipTests install

title: Support configuring readOnlyDataSource in LazyConnectionDataSourceProxy via auto-configuration
body:
**Description**
Spring Boot 4.1.0 introduces auto-configuration for `LazyConnectionDataSourceProxy`. However, there is currently no built-in way to configure a read-only data source for this proxy through auto-configuration or properties.

In scenarios where applications use separate ReadWriteDataSource (primary) and ReadOnlyDataSource (replica), the read-only data source is typically defined with `@Bean(defaultCandidate = false)`. To associate it with `LazyConnectionDataSourceProxy`, developers must manually define a custom DataSource bean and invoke setReadOnlyDataSource(...).

Providing first-class support for configuring the read-only data source via auto-configuration would eliminate this boilerplate and align with Spring Boot’s convention-over-configuration model.

Current WorkAround
```java
DataSource dataSource(final DataSource primaryDataSource, final @Qualifier("readOnly") DataSource replicaDataSource) {
    LazyConnectionDataSourceProxy proxy =
            new LazyConnectionDataSourceProxy(primaryDataSource);
    proxy.setReadOnlyDataSource(replicaDataSource);
    return proxy;
}
```

Can you please consider the Enhancement request

**Benefits**

- Eliminates manual bean configuration
- Simplifies multi-datasource (read/write split) setups
- Improves consistency with existing auto-configuration patterns

title: NimbusJwtDecoder silently accepts unknown values for spring.security.oauth2.resourceserver.jwt.jws-algorithms
body:
### Affects versions
3.5.x, 4.0.x, 4.x (main)

### Summary
`OAuth2ResourceServerJwtConfiguration.jwsAlgorithms(Set)` and its reactive counterpart `ReactiveOAuth2ResourceServerJwkConfiguration.jwsAlgorithms(Set)` map each configured value through `SignatureAlgorithm.from(String)` and add the result directly to the set:

```java
for (String algorithm : this.properties.getJwsAlgorithms()) {
    signatureAlgorithms.add(SignatureAlgorithm.from(algorithm));
}
```

`SignatureAlgorithm.from(String)` returns `null` when the argument is not a recognised algorithm, so the `null` is silently added to the set that is subsequently passed to `NimbusJwtDecoder` / `NimbusReactiveJwtDecoder`.

### Expected behavior
Consistent with the public-key path (`exactlyOneAlgorithm()` in the same class), an unknown algorithm name should fail fast at configuration time with an `InvalidConfigurationPropertyValueException` pointing at `spring.security.oauth2.resourceserver.jwt.jws-algorithms`, so the misconfiguration surfaces immediately.

### Actual behavior
A typo such as `RS265` (instead of `RS256`) is accepted silently and only surfaces later as a confusing verification-time failure at the first authenticated request.

### Suggested fix
Reject unknown algorithm names in both the servlet and reactive `jwsAlgorithms(Set)` methods using the same `InvalidConfigurationPropertyValueException` that `exactlyOneAlgorithm()` already uses. PR to follow against `3.5.x`.
